content.user_title: Inspect and Automate Chrome with OpenCLI
content.value_statement: Browser tasks often require page inspection, repeated interactions, and network evidence. This skill guides OpenCLI commands for Chrome sessions, authenticated pages, and native tab management.
actual_capabilities: Inspect page URLs, interactive element references, accessibility trees, and diagnostic state.
Locate elements and perform clicks, field entry, selections, uploads, keyboard input, and dialog interactions.
Extract page text or HTML, capture screenshots, and evaluate JavaScript in pages or selected frames.
Inspect captured request shapes, cached request details, raw response bodies, and static API candidates from loaded scripts.
Manage named page sessions, attach to the current user tab, and release bindings without closing that tab.
Discover native Chrome methods and organize tabs, groups, and windows using returned browser IDs.
limitations: Requires an available OpenCLI installation and a working Chrome connection; the skill does not include their implementations.
Bound sessions permit navigation but block tab creation, selection, and closure.
Static API candidates are not executed or proven; unresolved expressions and omitted scripts can limit analysis.
Network evidence can come from a recent cache rather than live capture; authenticated data and state-changing actions require authorized handling.

use_cases.title: Check Browser Form Behavior
use_cases.description: Inspect form controls, enter test values, and verify resulting page state in an authorized test environment.

use_cases.title: Investigate Frontend API Evidence
use_cases.description: Review observed request shapes and static script candidates while distinguishing live evidence, cached captures, and unresolved expressions.

use_cases.title: Organize Research Tabs
use_cases.description: Inspect open Chrome tabs and group selected research pages using actual browser IDs and supported native methods.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Open [URL] in a named OpenCLI session and report its title and interactive elements. Do not submit forms or change account data.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Test Form
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect [test URL], locate [field], enter [test value], and verify the field value. Refresh stale references and stop before submitting.

prompt_templates.title: Review Network Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect network evidence for [authorized page]. Summarize request shapes, cache provenance, and static candidates. Report incomplete analysis and exclude sensitive response bodies.

prompt_templates.title: Organize Native Chrome Tabs
prompt_templates.prompt: Discover supported native Chrome methods and permissions. List tabs, propose groups for [topic], then request approval before applying changes with actual browser IDs.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Inspect a page without changing account data.
output: No forms submitted and no account data changed.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Summarize API evidence and identify uncertainty.
output: Evidence source: recent cached capture; no live requests observed.
Request methods and response shapes summarized without raw response bodies.
Static script candidates remain unverified; unresolved expressions require further inspection.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Propose tab groups before making changes.
output: Research tabs identified from the current Chrome tab list.
Proposed group: Research, using the blue group color.
No browser changes applied; approval requested.

best_practices: Reuse a named session, consult command help, and refresh page state when element references become stale.
Check error outcomes and affected state before retrying writes; obtain approval for sensitive browser changes.
Inspect evidence provenance and analysis completeness; redact sensitive page content and raw network bodies before sharing.
anti_patterns: Treating static API candidates or cached captures as verified live behavior.
Reusing stale element references or substituting native Chrome IDs for session page identities.
Executing untrusted page JavaScript, sharing private response bodies, or changing account state without authorization.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides instructions for using OpenCLI browser commands. It does not bundle Chrome or the OpenCLI implementation.

faq.question: Can it work with logged-in sites?
faq.answer: It documents profile selection and attachment to the current user tab. Access depends on the available Chrome profile and permissions.

faq.question: Do all commands require a session?
faq.answer: Page commands require a named session. Native Chrome calls do not require a session or attach a page.

faq.question: Are static API candidates confirmed endpoints?
faq.answer: No. They are script analysis candidates, not executed or proven APIs. Check unresolved expressions, script errors, and analysis completeness.

faq.question: What happens when a write has an unknown outcome?
faq.answer: Inspect the affected state before retrying. The first attempt may already have changed the page or account.

faq.question: Does releasing a binding close my tab?
faq.answer: No. Unbind releases the attachment without closing the user tab. Native-created tabs and windows persist.
